newsitem.title: FRANCE: Referendum on Corsican independence suggested.
newsitem.headline: Referendum on Corsican independence suggested.

text.p: A French parliamentarian has called for a referendum on the troubled Mediterranean island of Corsica, saying it would show the great majority of its people wanted to stay French.

"I am among those who believe that a referendum is necessary in Corsica so the Corsicans can express their attitude towards integration with France," centre-rightist Patrick Devedjian said in a radio interview.
"I do not doubt for a single minute the answer would be 90 percent in favour of staying linked to France," said Devedjian, whose own constituency is near Paris.

"The referendum would be a very good answer to the autonomists who always claim to speak in the name of the Corsican people. It would de-legitimise them because it would demonstrate they act without popular support," he said.

Corsica has been the scene of hundreds of bombings by suspected separatist guerrillas in the past few years but few arrests have been made, largely because of the island's traditional "omerta" law of silence.

An opinion poll earlier this year showed 86 percent of the quarter-million Corsicans opposed independence but 49 percent expressed some sympathy for the nationalists, although they have never scored more than 20 percent in local elections.
The island was calm on Sunday after the formal end of a guerrilla truce already shattered by dozens of blasts.

The 10-month-old truce declared by the hardline Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC)-Historic Wing expired on Saturday but had already effectively lapsed when attacks resumed after secret talks with Paris broke down during the summer.
The most spectacular attack was a week ago against the town hall of the southwest France city of Bordeaux, whose mayor is Prime Minister Alain Juppe.
